chapter: Cab Calloway, Haiti and Sarah Vaughan
title: Discovering Sarah Vaughan at the Apollo amateur night
summary: Billy Eckstine and Budd persuade Earl Hines to hire a shabby young Sarah Vaughan after hearing her at the Apollo, and Hines buys her dresses.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: That's a most unusual trick. I'd like to ask you this and then -- because I don't want to --

Just digressing again, because we didn't get into, just digress back to the -- to the Billy Eckstine Earl Hines era, air There was a young girl named Sarah Vaughan that had -- you had a good deal of influence on, and you did a lot of things. Explain about when Sarah came into Earl's band and how and when you made some records together. Can you give us that, a little bit of that?
Yes. We had been playing the Appollo theater.

So -- in New York -- so after we played our week in the Apollo Theater, well, we had a week off. So, you know, the amateur nights was every Wednesday night in the Apollo theater. So Billy Eckstine had gone he knew all of the guys that would rehearse the amateurs and whatnot, and he was hanging around. We were living at the Braddock hotel.
126th and 8th Avenue. Earl was living around at the --
And Earl was living at the Theresa

Hotel, 125th and 7th Avenue. So Billy Eckstine ran up to the room and got me. He says, hey, man. He said, I just heard a little chick that can sing like a mocking bird. He said, look, she's goin' be on the amateur hour tonight, man. He says, you know, we should get Earl to hear this chick, man, and try to get her.

So we said, okay. I say, okay, B, come on. So we went around to Earl Hines' hotel at the Theresa Hotel, and told him, says, come on. I'm taking Billy at his word, because as great as Billy Eckstine is, if he tell me anybody can sing, I gotta believe him. So I helped Billy convince Earl. I says, come on, we're going to amateur night tonight, and we're going to hear this girl sing.

Okay, so we went to amateur night at the Appollo Theater, and here comes her turn, and this girl started to sing, and I'm telling you, right away we convinced Earl he should hire her. We went backstage and talked to this young girl and got her to agree to go with Earl Hines' band. Well, she was sort of shabby and didn't know how to dress or anything. Well, you know, Earl Hines.
And she wasn't the prettiest little thing, was she?
No, she wasn't the prettiest little girl, especially at that time. And, you know, of course, how dapper Earl always is, and he had -- he knew about clothes.

And he took her downtown and he bought her some dresses and things and talked to her mother and father and everything, and they let her go out on the road with us. So hence Sarah Vaughan. This was her first beginning with Earl Hines. And then, to our great discovery, she could play the piano, and she had played organ with the Newark Symphony Orchestra and studied with them, you know, when she was in high school. So when Earl find out this, he -- you know, he's an idea man -- right away he set up two pianos and Sarah played piano with the band and sung and like just clumped around or played, and the novelty of having like a piano facing Earl Hines and Sarah Vaughan to sing on one side and him on the other, and it was like show business.
